title: Attaché Intelligence Operations Technician (Attaché Intel Ops Tech)
raw_text:
8-351Z. Military Occupational Specialty 351Z--Attaché Intelligence Operations Technician
(Attaché Intel Ops Tech)
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
    b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21 and AR 611-60.
    c. MOS 351Z. MOS 351Z is an accession MOS. ALL enlisted MOS with SQI 7 (Attaché) are
eligible to apply. Applicants must have Defense Attaché Service experience.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. (Refer to Table 6-6 for list of Universal ASI associated with this MOS).
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
              (b) Possess a valid security clearance of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access to
Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI).
               (c) Complete the Attaché Intelligence Operations Technician MI Warrant Officer
Basic Course.
         (2) CW3 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
             (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Advanced Course (WOAC). (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate level Education (WOILE).
               (c) Complete the MI Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (MI WOILE).
         (3) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
               (c) Complete the MI Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (MI WOSSE).
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Leads joint operations and administrative support teams in Defense Attaché
Offices (DAO) at diplomatic missions worldwide.
               (b) Serves as principle advisor to the Senior Defense Official/Defense Attaché
(SDO/DATT) and ensures operations are conducted in accordance with requisite policies.
               (c) Represents the Department of Defense (DOD as diplomat and conducts liaison
with host nation and third country officials per diplomatic protocols.
               (d) Conducts inter-agency coordination with embassy partners to further DOD efforts
and advance US foreign-policy.
               (e) Synchronizes the DAO operations, performs management in support of strategic
reporting and ensures compliance with relevant regulations and policies.
               (f) Facilitates DOD activities in foreign countries by providing operational,
administrative, and logistical support to personnel caring out of DOD initiatives.
               (g) Serves as a key contributor to the embassy country team and advocates for DOD
equities.
               (h) Advises DOD personnel on embassy operations and inter-agency processes.
               (i) Plans and manages DAO Administration, policy compliance, finance personnel,
reporting, security and logistics.
        (2) CW3--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
               (b) Conducts inspections of both Defense Intelligence Agency internal elements and
Defense Intelligence Agency military personnel, and investigations as directed by the Defense
Intelligence Agency Inspector General.
        (3) CW4--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(2).
                (b) Implements DCSINT, DA, INSCOM, and Commander, FSC policies regarding the
administration of Army attaché personnel.
               (c) Coordinates policy with Defense Intelligence Agency and HRC; supervises the
activities of warrant officers, enlisted personnel, and DA civilians responsible for providing
administrative, personnel management, military pay, and Army representational support for Army
personnel serving in 90 countries who are affiliated with the Defense Attaché Systems; and
provides administrative management of the Army attaché and support staff personnel
procurement programs.
         (4) CW5 --
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(3).
               (b) MI Senior Field Grade Warrant Officers are proficient in the duties described for
Field Grade Warrant Officers in the duties paragraphs of one or more MI WO MOSs.
               (c) MI Senior Field Warrant Officers are branch technical experts and master-level
multidiscipline intelligence integrator, and advisor.
               (d) Provide direction, guidance, resources, assistance, and supervision necessary for
subordinates to perform duties.
               (e) Provide leader development, talent and lifecycle management, mentorship,
advice, and counsel to enlisted Soldiers, warrant officers, and branch officers and have special
warrant officer leadership and representation responsibilities within their respective commands.
               (f) Advise commanders and branch assignment managers on the assignments and
placement of Military Intelligence warrant officers world-wide.
               (g) Provide essential advice to commanders on warrant officer issues and perform
other officer level duties as required consistent with senior staff officer responsibilities.
               (h) May serve as the Senior WO advisor in MOS immaterial (011A) billets based on
technical knowledge and understanding of Army and Joint doctrine.
               (i) May serve on the Army Staff.
               (j) May serve as a Capabilities Branch Chief.
               (k) May serve as the MI WO Proponent.
               (l) May serve as the CCWO of the MI Branch.
               (m) MI Senior Field Grade Warrant Officers must have completed the WO Senior
Service Education Course prior to nomination for specified CW5 billets.
    g. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A physical profile of 222211.
         (3) Have normal color discrimination with corrected vision per one of the following three
categories of the good eye, bad eye categories: 20/40-20/70; 20/30-20/100; or, 20/20/400,
         (4) Have hearing wherein sound amplitude in one ear does not exceed 45 decibels at
frequencies 250, 500, 1000, and 2000 CPS (HZ) or 65 decibels at frequency 4000.
         (5) Qualifying Scores: A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) – 120 cm, seated
Power Throw (PT) – 350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 120 lbs, and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 36
shuttles in Physical Demands Category “Moderate” (Gold).
         (6) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed
in the following standards of grade table:
              (a) Table 8-351Z-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-351Z-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
